topic.title: Agent Identity & Agent Gateway
topic.docSection: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway & §5 Trigger #15
topic.summary: SPIFFE X.509 certificate identity, GCP IAM (BigQuery) vs user-delegated 3-legged OAuth (3P SaaS via auth manager), Agent Gateway ingress/egress governance + Model Armor with zero code changes.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 24
questions.q: What type of cryptographic identity does Google Cloud Agent Identity assign to each agent?
options: A dedicated SPIFFE-based identity with an X.509 certificate that is not shared and cannot be impersonated
A shared default Compute Engine service account JSON key
A static API key stored in an environment variable
A browser session cookie shared across all agents in the project
questions.why: Each agent gets its own SPIFFE-based identity with an X.509 certificate assigned by Google Cloud. It is not shared and cannot be impersonated.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 25
questions.q: When an agent queries a Google Cloud resource like BigQuery, which identity does it use?
options: The agent's own SPIFFE identity, governed by Google Cloud IAM
A 3-legged OAuth token issued by an external SaaS server
Its logical Agent Registry Identifier (urn:agent:...)
Agents never hold their own credential and must use an anonymous key
questions.why: For Google Cloud resources (like BigQuery), the agent uses its own SPIFFE identity governed by IAM. Watch out for the wrong option claiming 'an agent never holds its own credential.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 26
questions.q: An agent needs to create a Jira ticket in a third-party SaaS app on the user's behalf. How does it authenticate?
options: User-delegated 3-legged OAuth through the Agent Identity auth manager
The agent's own Google Cloud IAM service account
Hardcoding the user's credentials in the system prompt
Using an IAM deny policy on the BigQuery API
questions.why: When calling a third-party SaaS app on the user's behalf, the agent uses user-delegated 3-legged OAuth through the Agent Identity auth manager.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 26
questions.q: When an agent uses 3-legged OAuth via the Agent Identity auth manager to call a third-party SaaS API, who issues the access token?
options: The third-party SaaS OAuth server
Google Cloud IAM
Model Armor
BigQuery
questions.why: In user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for a third-party SaaS app, the token is issued by the SaaS OAuth server and managed by the Agent Identity auth manager.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slides 25–26
questions.q: In one workflow, an agent reads data from BigQuery and then updates a ticket in ServiceNow on the user's behalf. Which credentials does it use?
options: Its own SPIFFE identity (IAM) for BigQuery, and user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for ServiceNow
One combined credential that authenticates to both BigQuery and ServiceNow
User-delegated 3-legged OAuth for both BigQuery and ServiceNow
Its SPIFFE identity for ServiceNow, and 3-legged OAuth for BigQuery
questions.why: Classic §1.5 scenario: the agent uses its own SPIFFE identity (governed by IAM) for GCP resources like BigQuery, and user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for third-party SaaS apps.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 28
questions.q: Which traffic directions does Google Cloud Agent Gateway govern?
options: Both ingress (inbound to the agent) and egress (outbound from the agent to tools and other agents)
Egress traffic only
Ingress traffic only
Neither; Agent Gateway only handles token billing
questions.why: Agent Gateway governs both ingress and egress traffic and enforces access policies. Watch out for traps saying it 'only handles egress' or 'only billing.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 28
questions.q: A security team configures Agent Gateway with Model Armor to inspect an agent's tool calls and responses. What application code changes are required?
options: No application code changes are needed
Every tool function must be rewritten to call the Model Armor REST API manually
The agent must be migrated from Python to Go
Every prompt must be manually encrypted inside the agent code
questions.why: Agent Gateway is a fully managed component that governs ingress/egress traffic, enforces access policies, and integrates with Model Armor to inspect tool calls and responses with no app code changes needed.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slides 24–29
questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between Agent Gateway and Agent Identity?
options: Agent Gateway works alongside and requires Agent Identity; it does not replace Agent Identity
Agent Gateway replaces Agent Identity so agents no longer need SPIFFE certificates
Agent Gateway and Agent Identity cannot be used together
Agent Gateway is a container runtime that replaces Cloud Run and GKE
questions.why: Watch out for the trap 'Gateway replaces Agent Identity.' Agent Gateway is a managed ingress/egress control point that works alongside Agent Identity.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 & Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 25
questions.q: When deploying an agent to Agent Runtime, when can Agent Identity (--agent-identity) be enabled?
options: Only when the agent is created
Only after the agent is deleted
Automatically whenever a file over 4 MB is uploaded
Only on third-party on-premises servers
questions.why: On Agent Runtime, Agent Identity (--agent-identity) is immutable after creation and can only be enabled when the agent is first created.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 & Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 29
questions.q: Why must a container image trust AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES when bound to an egress Agent Gateway?
options: Because an egress Agent Gateway performs TLS decryption and inspection on outbound agent traffic
Because BigQuery requires client-side TLS certificates for SQL syntax parsing
Because Agent Registry stores skill files inside X.509 certificates
Because OAuth tokens are compiled into the Dockerfile at build time
questions.why: An egress Agent Gateway performs TLS inspection (with Model Armor) on outbound communications, so the container image must trust the gateway's root CA.
